 Order

This appeal by the Insurance Company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 04.03.2022 passed by I Additional MACT, Neemuch in Claim Case No.59/2020.
2.

Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company, after referring to MLC Ex.P-5, statement Ex.D-3 and other evidence on record, submits that, in the instant case, it is established that deceased was sitting on tractor trolley and came under the tractor trolley after the same turned upside down.
Therefore, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
It is also urged that Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased on higher side and has awarded excessive compensation.
Hence, appeal be allowed and Insurance Company be exonerated from the liability to pay compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent submits that findings recorded by the Tribunal are well supported by evidence on record.
There is no illegality or perversity in the findings recorded by the Tribunal.
Hence, appeal be dismissed.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

5. So far as liability of Insurance Company to pay compensation is concerned, it is correct that in MLC Ex.P-5 it is mentioned "Alleged H/o fall from Tractor Troli and comes below Troli near Chaldu around 9:15 AM on 13/06/20" and Ex.D-3 is statement of claimant Rajaram, recorded by Investigator of Insurance Company.
Perusal of Ex.P-5 reveals that therein it is mentioned that deceased was brought by one Omprakash, but this Omprakash has not been examined in the case.
It is also not clear as to who informed Dr. Amit that deceased Ajay fell from tractor trolley.

Further,
Dr.Amit, who prepared Ex.P-5 MLC has also not been examined.
Therefore, just in view of entry in MLC Ex.P-5, it cannot be said that at the time of accident, deceased was sitting on tractor trolley and he fell from tractor trolley.
Further, deposition of claimant Rajaram reveal that he has not controverted/contradicted with Ex.D- 3's statement.
Therefore, Ex.D-3's statement cannot be used to show that at the time of accident, deceased was travelling in tractor trolley and he fell from tractor trolley.

6. In view of above and perusal of overall evidence on record reveal that in the instant case, it is not established that at the time of accident deceased was travelling in tractor trolley and he fell from tractor trolley.

Therefore, it cannot be said that findings recorded by Tribunal on above issue are Shri Ram General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Rajaram Bavari on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163008062/
2 perverse or against evidence on record.

sentences.text: 7. So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, it is apparent from para 32 of the impugned award that Tribunal has determined monthly income of the deceased treating him as unskilled labour and has fixed his salary on the basis of minimum wages.
It is well settled that when there is no documentary evidence to prove monthly income of deceased, then, it can be fixed on the basis of minimum wages.
Hence, on above issue also no fault can be found with the findings of the Tribunal and it cannot be said that Tribunal has awarded compensation excessively.
8. In view of discussion in the foregoing paras, in this Court's considered opinion, there is no illegality or perversity in the impugned award.
Hence, appeal being devoid of merit is hereby dismissed.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE RJ Shri Ram General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Rajaram Bavari on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163008062/
